content:
Folding screens tend to develop more visible creases over time, but Apple’s Kate Bergeron says the foldable iPhone Duo uses a replaceable protective layer to help address this issue.

The "protective layer" on the foldable iPhone Duo’s folding display can be replaced over time, keeping it in like-new condition for longer

Following the unveiling of the foldable iPhone Duo last month, Apple executives sat down for an interview to explain why the company has deliberately focused on maximising durability and minimising the crease issues common to other foldables.

One of these efforts appears to be a unique design feature on the foldable iPhone Duo that ensures users can maintain that "first day out of the box" experience for years to come: a replaceable protective layer on the folding screen.

Below is the interview with Apple’s VP of Hardware Engineering, Kate Bergeron, conducted by TikTok user @angietutorials:

Top comment from OrangeQuill

Knowing that they felt the need to do this makes me even more worried about how durable it will actually end up being. Hopefully they’re just being overly cautious, and not setting us up for insane out-of-warranty repair costs without AppleCare.

The full clip can be seen on TikTok.

Apple mentions this "protective layer" in their iPhone Duo AppleCare estimated repair cost table. As spotted by Quinn Nelson, the cost to replace the protective layer under AppleCare is $19. Without AppleCare, the cost is currently unknown.

So if you’re worried about spending over $2,000 on an iPhone Duo only for the screen crease to become more pronounced over time, it looks like Apple already has a solution in place.

Are you worried about the crease issue on the iPhone Duo? Let us know in the comments.
